slice: A05 OIDC — login, linking, collision and the second factor on a local provider
verdict: SC1 SC2 SC3 SC5 PASS; SC4 FAIL (second factor not applied on a provider login); SC6 PASS

primary.client: one staticClient, redirect URI http://127.0.0.1:8099/api/v1/auth/oauth/dex/callback, skipApprovalScreen true
primary.why_not_keycloak: Dex's static connector expresses as many users with distinct or colliding emails as needed; the collision this row cares about is between a provider identity and a LOCAL password account, not between two provider users. What Dex cannot express is email_verified:false — it always asserts verified — so the unverified case moved to the hostile fixture rather than to Keycloak.

hostile.what: ≈140-line stdlib-only OIDC provider written for this lab
hostile.shape: one issuer per mode under /p/<mode>, each with its own discovery document, JWKS and RS256 signer, so one core boot could be pointed at all of them
hostile.why: a correct provider can never produce a wrong nonce, a foreign issuer, a foreign signing key or an unverified email

lab.core: branch a05/oidc off 03ac3e8, two processes (VIDRA_ROLE=api on :8088, a separate VIDRA_ROLE=worker), schema 143
lab.postgres: native postgresql@16.15 on 127.0.0.1:55477, socket /tmp/voidc, migrated from EMPTY to 143
lab.flags: RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false, MALWARE_SCAN_MODE=disabled, HTTP_IMPORT_ALLOW_PRIVATE_URLS=false, MFA_KEY_KEK set, DEV_MAIL_CAPTURE_ENABLED=true only for the reset-remedy probe
lab.ssrf_guard: OIDC discovery/JWKS/token traffic does NOT pass the URL-import SSRF guard — OAuthService.httpClient is a plain http.Client with a 15s timeout — so the loopback issuer needed no dev knob

query: redirect_uri (derived from PUBLIC_BASE_URL, never from a request parameter)

sc1_state_matrix.signature-valid cookie sealed 11 minutes: 400 — the age is checked server-side, not only by Max-Age
sc1_state_matrix.happy path: 302 to the validated return_to, vidra_refresh set

sc1_username_derivation.rule: UsernameExists probes actor_handles, not users — accounts and channels share one namespace (migration 0142)
sc1_username_derivation.measured: a channel handle 'labchan' existed; the provider identity whose name claim was 'labchan' became username 'labchan2'

sc1_config_refusals.provider named, _CLIENT_SECRET missing: boot refused: config: OAUTH_DEX_CLIENT_SECRET is required
sc1_config_refusals.provider named, no variables at all: boot refused, all three reported at once
sc1_config_refusals.provider named, PUBLIC_BASE_URL empty: boot refused: PUBLIC_BASE_URL must be a valid http(s) origin when OAUTH_PROVIDERS is set
sc1_config_refusals.OAUTH_PROVIDERS unset: instance.oauth_providers = [], login page renders no provider buttons, begin answers 404 (not 503), /me/oauth-identities still 200 with an empty list, unlink 404

sc2_email_collision.setup: password account pwcollide / collide@lab.test, locally email_verified=false
sc2_email_collision.provider: Dex asserting the same address with email_verified:true
sc2_email_collision.outcome: LINKED to the existing account and signed in as it; no second account created (user count unchanged); audit row auth.oauth.link success oauth:dex
sc2_email_collision.unverified variant: refused with ?oauth_error=email_conflict, no session, no account created
sc2_email_collision.observation: the local email_verified stays false after the link — SetUserEmailVerified runs only on the account-creation path
sc2_email_collision.cross_provider_takeover: a SECOND configured provider asserting email_verified:true for labowner@lab.test signed in as the instance OWNER (role admin, is_owner true). There is no per-provider email-domain restriction: every configured provider can claim every local account whose address it is willing to assert.

sc3_link_unlink.cross-user unlink: not addressable — the route is /me/oauth-identities/:provider, scoped to the principal, so there is no IDOR surface
sc3_link_unlink.OIDC-only account, unlink last method: 422 'cannot remove the last sign-in method — set a password first'
sc3_link_unlink.relink: signing in through the provider again re-creates the row with a new created_at
sc3_link_unlink.422 remedy is real for OIDC: password-reset on the passwordless OIDC account: request 202, confirm 204, password login issues a session, unlink then 204 — unlike ATProto, whose synthetic @atproto.invalid address makes the same remedy impossible
sc3_link_unlink.no link-from-settings: ConnectedLogins lists and unlinks only; /settings/connections is outbound cross-posting. The callback is session-blind: a signed-in user who authenticates as a different provider user is silently switched to that other account (measured newcomer -> mfauser).

sc4_second_factor.setup: one account with a password, TOTP enrolled and verified, and a linked Dex identity
sc4_second_factor.mechanism: auth/oauth.go calls Service.issueTokens at three sites and auth/atproto.go at two; only Service.Login consults mfaEnabled
sc4_second_factor.verdict: the second factor is bypassed by every provider login path; recorded, not fixed — the fix needs a challenge over a top-level redirect (a new transport for the mfa_token), which is a contract change across core and user, not a surgical edit

sc5_outage.boot with a dead issuer: succeeds — discovery is lazy, so an unreachable IdP delays only login attempts
sc5_outage.begin, no cached discovery, issuer down: 502 oauth_provider_unavailable (this slice's fix; it was an untyped server_error before)
sc5_outage.begin, discovery already cached, issuer: 302 to the dead issuer — the browser fails at the IdP; vidra cannot know without probing
sc5_outage.discovery cache: per-process and in-memory, so it does NOT survive a restart
sc5_outage.sealed credentials: none — the client secret is plain configuration, read at boot
